clone.accidental: copy-paste that should be shared; a maintainer would accept extracting a helper
clone.deliberate: kept on purpose: platform/runtime variants, data tables, versioned copies, decoupling across boundaries, performance, parallel structure (one file per locale or adapter)
clone.inconsistent: the copies differ in a way that looks like a fix, guard or behavior applied to one copy only: a likely bug
clone.trivial: tiny or idiomatic repetition not worth sharing

dead-store.debug-wip: debug scaffolding or work in progress
dead-store.bug: the lost value should have been used; concrete consequence
dead-store.false-positive: the value is read (closures, try/finally, loops)
dead-store.intentional: deliberate: clearing a reference for GC, readability/narrowing initializer, documented defensive reset
dead-store.leftover: harmless redundancy, safe to delete: an initializer always overwritten, a redundant reset

export.analysis-miss: a static reference exists that the analysis missed
export.dead: nothing uses it and it isn't public; deletable
export.dynamic: used by name at runtime (registry, string-keyed lookup, virtual module)
export.public-api: public surface: documented, re-exported, module augmentation, deliberate wildcard subpath
export.test-or-tooling: used only by tests, scripts, build config or docs
export.unnecessary-export: declaration live in its own file or via a side effect (self-registration); only `export` is unneeded

unused.debug-wip: debug scaffolding or work in progress
unused.bug: the value was computed or received and should have been used (wrong variable, typo, lost result, ignored option); concrete runtime consequence
unused.intentional: signature placeholder, interface-conformance or API-compat parameter, destructuring omit, `_` convention, type-level trick, catch binding kept by style
